content: The Incidence and Prevalence Project aims to establish the largest open-source repository of published epidemiological data globally. WikiDoc intends to use this data to assist patients in understanding their likelihood of developing specific diseases or conditions. This initiative is designed for individuals at various educational levels, including high school, college, medical school, and doctoral programs, to contribute their expertise. Participants will need to develop proficiency in conducting academic research and calculating disease prevalence based on published data. WikiDoc encourages participation in this project. The goals of the Incidence and Prevalence Project include the following: 1. To compile the largest open-source repository of published prevalence data for rare diseases. 2. To help patients understand and quantify their risk of developing specific diseases or conditions. 3. To generate data that can support the development of artificial intelligence systems for disease diagnosis. The project is open to editors at the Assistant Editor-in-Chief level or higher. It is specifically designed for students at all levels (high school, college, medical school, and doctoral programs) to refine their quantitative research skills. If you are interested in participating in the Incidence and Prevalence Project, you can email WikiDoc to receive your assigned portion of the prevalence database to research. The next steps for participation are as follows: 1. A member of the WikiDoc team will provide you with a research assignment. Begin by opening your spreadsheet. 2. Identify a disease in column B. Diseases in blue font should be ignored. 3. Determine the prevalence of the disease in terms of cases per 100,000 using reputable sources such as the World Health Organization, the Centers for Disease Control, the National Institutes of Health, or the Clinton Foundation. When possible, find prevalence data for both developed countries (column C) and developing/undeveloped countries (column D). Use the provided link to determine whether a country is classified as developed or developing. Prevalence is defined as the total number of cases of a disease in a given population at a specific time. In some cases, prevalence data can be directly obtained from a source. In other cases, it may need to be converted into the format of cases per 100,000. For example, if a source reports 20 cases per 1,000, this should be converted to 2,000 cases per 100,000 and entered as 2,000 in the appropriate column. If prevalence data is not available for a particular disease, it can be calculated by dividing the number of reported cases by the population size in which those cases were reported. Multiply the result by 100,000 to express the statistic in cases per 100,000. For example, if there are X reported cases in a population of Y, the prevalence is calculated as (X/Y) × 100,000. Enter this value in column C. All calculations should be performed in the Excel sheet using basic Excel functions. Additionally, provide a brief explanation of the calculation in column E. This explanation should include the number of cases and the population size used in the calculation. For example: The prevalence was calculated by dividing the X number of reported cases by the Y population of country Z and multiplying by 100,000. Enter the sources of your information in columns F and G. Ensure that another researcher could independently verify your calculations using only the sources you provide and the explanation of the calculations you performed. Save your completed spreadsheet with the filename format Prevalence_YourInitials.xlsx, replacing YourInitials with your actual initials. Email the completed spreadsheet to WikiDoc (wikidoc@wikidoc.org). If you have any questions, please ask before proceeding. Kristin is available via telephone Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM EST, at 617-632-7590, or via email at wikidoc@wikidoc.org.
